title: He obeyed… but not completely.
paragraphs: And God said, that’s enough to stop you.

You can be called…
and still be in danger.

You can be chosen…
and still be out of alignment.

You can carry a destiny…
and still be hiding disobedience.

A bush that burned but was not consumed.
A voice that shook the ground beneath his excuses.
A calling that would rewrite history.

“Go back to Egypt.”
“Set My people free.”

No crowd.
No spotlight.
No applause.

What could be so serious…
that the same God who called him…
would confront him like an enemy?
Here’s the part we don’t like to preach.
The part that hits too close.
“At a lodging place on the way the LORD met him and sought to put him to death.” — Exodus 4:24

Something raw.
Something desperate.
Something bloody.
“Then Zipporah took a flint knife and cut off her son’s foreskin and touched Moses’ feet with it and said, ‘Surely you are a bridegroom of blood to me!’ So He let him alone.” — Exodus 4:25–26
God had already spoken generations before:
“Every male among you shall be circumcised… it shall be a sign of the covenant between me and you.” — Genesis 17:10–11
Some scholars interpret that Moses delayed circumcising his son because of cultural pressure from his Midianite surroundings… or tension in his household.
But Scripture is clear about one thing:
Was disobeying the God of Israel.
This is where it gets personal.
We love saying, “God is using me.”
But we don’t always love full obedience.

“I’ll follow…
but let me keep this part.”
But in the kingdom of God?
God may let you move for a while…
But He will confront what you refuse to surrender.
But because He loves you too much to let you lead in hypocrisy.
Moses was about to stand before Pharaoh.
The one you say, “It’s not that serious.”
Because the Holy Spirit has already whispered it.
Now here’s where the story turns.
And this is the part that will break you… and heal you.
This isn’t just a strange Old Testament moment.
A prophetic whisper of something greater.
“But He was pierced for our transgressions; He was crushed for our iniquities… and by His wounds we are healed.” — Isaiah 53:5
Jesus didn’t come with partial obedience.
“He humbled Himself by becoming obedient to the point of death—even death on a cross.” — Philippians 2:8
Where Moses almost died for his disobedience…
Jesus chose to die for yours.
“For the wages of sin is death, but the gift of God is eternal life in Christ Jesus our Lord.” — Romans 6:23
You don’t clean yourself up to come to God.
Grace is not permission to stay the same.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us our sins and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.” — 1 John 1:9
What is God asking you to surrender?
Because the same God who confronted Moses…
Is the same God who sent Jesus.
Not because you’re afraid of punishment—
But because you’ve seen His love.
And His love is too real…
Because the calling on your life is real.
You don’t have to choose between them.

“Lord, no more partial obedience.
I surrender everything.
Cleanse me. Change me. Lead me.
I choose You—fully.”
